name: Are my files uploaded when editing metadata?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Metadata editing is processed entirely in your browser using pdf-lib. Files never leave your device.

name: Does PDFree store or log my files after processing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. PDFree runs entirely in your browser — there is no backend server that receives your files. Because nothing is uploaded, nothing can be stored, logged, or retained. Your document exists only in your browser's memory for the duration of the session and is cleared when you close the tab.

name: What metadata fields does PDFree show and edit?

acceptedAnswer.text: PDFree reads and writes the standard PDF document information dictionary: Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Creator (application that created the PDF), and Producer (PDF library used). Modification date is updated automatically on save.

name: Can I remove all metadata from a PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can clear any or all metadata fields before saving. This is useful for removing personal information before sharing a document.

name: Does editing metadata change the PDF content or appearance?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Metadata is stored separately from page content. Editing or clearing metadata fields has zero effect on text, images, layout, or any visible element of the document.

name: Does removing metadata reduce file size?

acceptedAnswer.text: Slightly — metadata is a small part of the PDF structure. The size reduction is negligible for most files but may be a few kilobytes.

name: Can I see all the metadata currently in my PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. When you upload a PDF, PDFree reads and displays all existing metadata values in the form fields. Empty fields mean that data is not present in the file.

name: Is there metadata that PDFree cannot edit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. XMP metadata packets (extended metadata embedded by some Adobe products) and custom application-specific metadata may not be editable. PDFree edits the standard PDF info dictionary which covers the most common fields.
